Several AI models were released in mid-October 2026. The most recent I found is Meta's open-weight Muse Spark Open, which one tracker lists as released October 15. It is Meta's new open-weight model for coding and agent tasks, which Meta calls the most capable US open-weight model so far. The weights are free to download, and Meta worked with Apple so it can run locally on a pair of Mac Studios.

Other October releases I found:

- **NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL** (October 15): an open-weights model, per one comparison table.
- **Google Gemini 4 Argon** (October 13): Google's newest frontier model is now broadly available, after launching only to vetted cyber defenders. A separate table lists it as announced September 30 with availability on October 13.
- **xAI Grok Voice 3.0** (October 14): one aggregator lists this as the newest release in its database.
- **Meta Muse Wonder 1.0** (October 12): one source says Meta's top Muse Wonder models stay closed, while Muse Spark Open is the open-weight release.
- **Anthropic Claude Haiku 5.5** (October 7) and **OpenAI GPT-6** (rolled out to ChatGPT users around October 7, per one tracker).

Caveats:
- The sources disagree on details. The release lists differ from one another, and some of the sites appear to be aggregators or blogs rather than official announcements. I'd check the providers' own blogs or announcements before relying on exact dates.
- Several of the sources are a few days old, and today is October 18, so newer releases may exist that I didn't find.

This week (October 12-18, 2026), Meta was the clear headline launcher. Google had a general-availability milestone, and I found no confirmed new flagship from OpenAI or Anthropic in this window. Some sources are aggregators that disagree on dates, so I've noted those conflicts.

**Meta (biggest launch this week)**
- Meta launched a new family of models that it says can compete at the frontier, with Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on Monday, October 12. Meta positioned them against OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.
- Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, while the more capable Muse Wonder Full is available to Muse Code subscribers.
- Pricing reported for Muse Wonder was $4/$20, per one blog, and a monthly subscription ranging from $20 to $100, per Euronews.
- Meta then released an open-weights model. Meta released Muse Spark Open on Thursday, the open-weights version of its Muse Spark model. One source describes it as a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 816 billion total parameters.

**Google**
- Google released its latest flagship model Gemini 4 Argon on October 1 with full dev access given only on October 13. Another source says Google has made Gemini 4 Argon generally available worldwide. Treat the October 13 date as the week's news and the October 1 date as the original launch.

**Anthropic**
- The most recent Anthropic model I found, Claude Haiku 5.5, launched October 7, which is before this window.
- Anthropic's Claude Code 2.1.302 release on October 17 added client-side automatic model selection and new idle-compaction controls. This is a tooling update, not a new model.

**OpenAI**
- I did not find a confirmed OpenAI model launch dated October 12-18. The most recent ones listed are from late September, such as GPT-6.1 Sol Pro API launch on September 29.
- One article says OpenAI released GPT-5.3-Codex this month, but it doesn't give a specific date, so I can't place it in this week.

**Other notable releases this week:** NVIDIA released three open AI models, Nemotron, per one news brief. Also, Jais 3 (IFM) and Grok Voice 3.0 (xAI) appeared in trackers for the past week.

If you want, I can search for OpenAI-specific announcements from this week or check the official Meta and Google blogs to confirm dates.

content.text:
Here are the three biggest AI model releases from the past week (Oct 11–18, 2026):

1. **Meta Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full (Oct 12):** Meta released a new closed family of models it pitches as competing at the frontier with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google; Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, and Muse Wonder Full is for Muse Code subscribers. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/12/meta-new-ai-models-anthropic-openai)

2. **Meta Muse Spark Open (Oct 15):** Meta released a free-to-download, open-weight model for coding and agent tasks, reported as an 816-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, which Meta calls the most capable US open-weight model yet. [DEV Community digest](https://dev.to/hiroki-ii-ai/ai-daily-digest-october-17-2026-meta-opens-816b-parameters-chatgpt-drives-chrome-anthropic-3pij)

3. **Google Gemini 4 Argon goes generally available (Oct 13):** Google's newest frontier model became broadly available after first being offered only to vetted cyber defenders. [Clone Systems](https://www.clone-systems.com/blog/new-ai-models-october-2026-release-guide-and-security)

Things to know:
- Gemini 4 Argon was first announced around Sept 30 to Oct 1, so what happened this week is that it opened up to everyone, not a brand-new announcement.
- The sources disagree on some dates. Links 2 and 3 are a news digest and a vendor blog, not official announcements, so check Meta's and Google's own blogs before relying on exact details.
- I left out Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 because both came out around Oct 7, just outside the 7-day window. Another candidate this week was NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (Oct 15).
